newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh state oil firm won't hurt j/ventures - PM.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh state oil firm won't hurt j/ventures - PM.

text.p: Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said on Wednesday that the creation of a new state oil company in place of the former Soviet republic's energy ministry would not affect existing joint ventures.

"In no way can this even be suggested," Kazhegeldin told a news conference in the Kazakh capital Almaty, responding to investors' fears that the new state company, Kazakh Oil, might adversely affect the operations of existing ventures with foreign oil companies.

Investors in the oil-rich Central Asian state have been worried by a shake-up in the government, in which Kazhegeldin appeared to have lost out in a struggle with the country's oil barons over the pace of privatising the energy sector.
Of particular concern was the creation of a new state-owned oil company, Kazakh Oil, in place of the ministry of oil and gas. Kazakh Oil would hold 40-50 percent stakes in all energy ventures.
The former oil and gas minister and new head of Kazakh Oil, Nurlan Balgimbayev, and oil enterprise directors oppose foreign control of the industry.

Kazhegeldin said existing deals with oil majors like Chevron Corp, Amoco Corp and Mobil Corp would not be affected by the restructuring. "The government had many different holdings and we are now putting them under the control of one company," the prime minister said.
